summary: Keep cancellation signalling live exec descendants when unrelated processes exit during observation

replay.detail: No replay or migration. Existing recorded kill results are not rewritten.

schema.detail: No graph, database or exec generation schema changes.

rules.detail: Admission, canonical ordering and checkpoint rules are unchanged.

compatibility.detail: Previously, live hosts could leave a cancelled gate's processes running after reporting its kill as successful. On Linux, a process reaped between opening and reading its proc stat entry is now skipped during process-group observation, just like an already absent entry. Stop and kill operations return an error when the exec generation is indeterminate, so callers cannot certify a signal that was skipped. Generation fences and process-group containment remain unchanged. Shutdown attempts both signal phases for every owned exec and reports collected errors after the sweep, so one unreadable generation cannot leave the remaining execs unsignalled.

downtime.detail: None beyond the normal daemon binary replacement.

recovery.detail: New cancellation attempts can finish group teardown despite unrelated process exits. Genuinely unreadable generation evidence remains an error rather than a successful teardown. Previously recorded kill results are retained. Shutdown continues tearing down other owned execs when one generation cannot be verified.
